newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr's rise due to rate-gap speculation--Japan gov't.
newsitem.headline: Dlr's rise due to rate-gap speculation--Japan gov't.

text.p: The dollar's rise on Monday was due to market speculation that the gap between Japanese and U.S. interest rates will expand, Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.

"I understand that dollar buying was prompted by speculation that the gap between Japanese and U.S. interest rates will widen after the announcement (last Friday) of the U.S. employment data," Kajiyama said. He did not make any further reference to exchange rates.
The dollar rose to a 50-month high of 124.98 yen in Tokyo morning trading on Monday.

The United States announced on Friday that its unemployment rate dipped in March to 5.2 percent from 5.3 percent in February, seeming to indicate a tighter labour market and fuelling speculation that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates again.
